verses.text: Once again David gathered all the best soldiers of Israel, thirty thousand men.
David and all his men set out from Baale Judah to bring up God's ark from there. The ark is called by the Name, the name of the LORD of Armies, who sits on his throne above the winged creatures.
They put God's ark on a new cart and brought it out of Abinadab's house on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio, Abinadab's sons, were guiding the new cart.
They brought it out of Abinadab's house on the hill with God's ark on it, and Ahio walked in front of the ark.
David and all the people of Israel were celebrating in front of the LORD with all kinds of instruments made of cypress wood: harps, lyres, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.
When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of God's ark.
The LORD's anger burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down there because of what he had done wrong. He died there beside God's ark.
David was upset because the LORD had burst out in anger against Uzzah. He named that place Perez Uzzah, and it is still called that today.
David was afraid of the LORD that day, and he said, "How can the LORD's ark ever come to me?"
So David would not take the LORD's ark into the City of David to be with him. Instead he took it aside to the house of Obed-Edom from Gath.
The LORD's ark stayed in the house of Obed-Edom from Gath for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-Edom and his whole family.

King David was told, "The LORD has blessed Obed-Edom's family and everything he has, because of God's ark." So David went and brought God's ark up from Obed-Edom's house to the City of David with great joy.
When the men carrying the LORD's ark had taken six steps, David sacrificed an ox and a fat calf.
David danced in front of the LORD with all his strength. He was wearing a linen ephod, a priest's apron.
So David and all the people of Israel brought up the LORD's ark with shouts of joy and the sound of trumpets.
As the LORD's ark came into the City of David, Michal, Saul's daughter, looked out of a window. She saw King David leaping and dancing in front of the LORD, and she hated him in her heart.
They brought in the LORD's ark and put it in its place inside the tent David had set up for it. Then David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings in front of the LORD.
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Armies.
Then he gave food to everyone in the whole crowd of Israel, both men and women. Each person got a loaf of bread, a cake of dates, and a cake of raisins. Then all the people went home.

When David went home to bless his family, Michal, Saul's daughter, came out to meet him. She said, "How great the king of Israel looked today! He uncovered himself in front of his servants' slave girls, like a foolish man with no shame!"

David said to Michal, "I did it in front of the LORD. He chose me instead of your father or anyone from his family, and he made me ruler over the LORD's people Israel. So I will celebrate in front of the LORD.
I will make myself look even more foolish than this, and I will be humble in my own eyes. But those slave girls you spoke about will honour me."
And Michal, Saul's daughter, had no children for the rest of her life.
